title: Do not assume a running audit UI process picks up a src/ui/server.js edit. index.html is read fresh
trigger: editing src/ui/server.js (adding or changing a route/handler) while an audit UI process is already running, or verifying a UI change against a live instance
behavior_delta: Do not assume a running audit UI process picks up a src/ui/server.js edit. index.html is read fresh from disk on every GET '/' request (src/ui/server.js), so front-end changes show up on a browser refresh with no restart. Route/handler logic, by contrast, is only the code loaded into the Node process at startup — a new endpoint (e.g. an SSE route) or a changed handler returns 404 or old behavior against an already-running process until that process is restarted. When verifying a server-side change, start a fresh process (or confirm the live one was restarted after the edit) rather than trusting a live reload.
what: Do not assume a running audit UI process picks up a src/ui/server.js edit. index.html is read fresh from disk on every GET '/' request (src/ui/server.js), so front-end changes show up on a browser refresh with no restart. Route/handler logic, by contrast, is only the code loaded into the Node process at startup — a new endpoint (e.g. an SSE route) or a changed handler returns 404 or old behavior against an already-running process until that process is restarted. When verifying a server-side change, start a fresh process (or confirm the live one was restarted after the edit) rather than trusting a live reload.
why: Verified this in-session: added GET /api/events to src/ui/server.js, then tested against the project's own already-running audit UI process and got a 404, while a freshly started instance on a different port served it correctly (200, working SSE stream). The two files degrade differently and it is easy to misread a stale-process 404 as a code bug.

evidence_refs.summary: index.html is readFile'd per request (line ~65); routes are handled by the createServer callback installed once at startup.
